errata.locus: note ²² ("Brave Emily clothed in Barefoot Rank"), allusion (1)
errata.was: (1) Emily Dickinson, whose "Barefoot Rank" compresses Poem 263 — "Barefoot Rank" is NOT a Dickinson phrase; it is Damascus's own compression of her posture: barefoot (uncredentialed) yet ranked (aristocratic).
errata.now: (1) Emily Dickinson, whose phrase it is: "My Barefoot-Rank is better —", in her letter to T. W. Higginson of 7 June 1862 (Johnson L265), the letter that declines to hurry into print. The Epistle names her and clothes her in her own phrase: barefoot (uncredentialed) yet ranked. The same letter is quoted entire in item 23 of "Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose" (Pearl and Other Poems, 2014), the Epistle's companion text of the same year.
errata.reason: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-28: "of course barefoot rank is a dickinson phrase. the epistle says so itself." The phrase is Dickinson's: L265, "My Barefoot-Rank is better —".
